instruction: The great Mayan king Pacal built temples in the city of Palenque in order to:
input:
Options:
A. satisfy the powerful Mayan astronomer priests.
B. display his generosity to the common people, since they were allowed to live in the temples.
C. frighten away enemies, in particular the Spaniards.
D. legitimize his kingship, since his father was not royal.
output: D. legitimize his kingship, since his father was not royal.

instruction: According to Timothy Pauketat, the evidence for social stratification and political power at Cahokia suggests:
input:
Options:
A. a center of Mississippian civilization with conditions similar to the rise of early states.
B. the limitations of authority in a Native American society of egalitarian foragers.
C. a simple chiefdom or perhaps a complex chiefdom had evolved by A.D. 1500.
D. a center of Mississippian civilization with conditions similar to societies on the Northwest Coast of North America.
output: A. a center of Mississippian civilization with conditions similar to the rise of early states.

instruction: Researchers now believe that the decline of the Maya was caused chiefly by:
input:
Options:
A. a cataclysm of some kind, such as an earthquake, volcano, or tsunami.
B. ecological degradation resulting from slash-and-burn farming techniques.
C. endless wars between neighboring Mayan city-states.
D. practices of interbreeding that led to a steep rise in congenital disorders.
output: B. ecological degradation resulting from slash-and-burn farming techniques.

instruction: Recent research on hominid species dating from the Middle Pliocene indicates there was (as of 2020):
input:
Options:
A. a great amount of species diversity, or a single species that exhibited a lot of diversity.
B. very little species diversity during this period and very few hominids.
C. decreased species diversity due to a prolonged ice age followed by a severe drought.
D. decreased species diversity but increased numbers of hammerstones and flakes, indicating stone tool manufacture.
output: A. a great amount of species diversity, or a single species that exhibited a lot of diversity.

instruction: What is the approximate mean cranial capacity of Homo erectus?
input:
Options:
A. under 650 cc
B. about 800 cc
C. just under 1000 cc
D. 1200 cc
output: C. just under 1000 cc

instruction: Why did the Mogollon leave their mountain homeland?
input:
Options:
A. disease
B. warfare
C. drought
D. all of the above
output: C. drought

instruction: Part of the Inca political strategy included all of the following EXCEPT:
input:
Options:
A. bringing the rulers of subdued provinces to live in the capital city.
B. building administrative centers in the capitals of the states they subdued.
C. building vast systems of roads.
D. the ritual sacrifice of captives of war to appease the sun god.
output: D. the ritual sacrifice of captives of war to appease the sun god.

instruction: Mesopotamia is located between which two rivers?
input:
Options:
A. Amazon and Nile
B. Euphrates and Nile
C. Tigris and Euphrates
D. Thames and Danube
output: C. Tigris and Euphrates

instruction: Among Inca royalty, what happened following the death of the king?
input:
Options:
A. the king's body was mummified and treated as if it were alive
B. hundreds of the elite were sacrificed by ritual decapitation
C. the body was entombed with lavish burial goods within an enormous pyramid
D. all of the above
output: A. the king's body was mummified and treated as if it were alive

instruction: Recent discoveries at the Cuncaicha rockshelter and Pucuncho quarry site provide evidence for which of the following?
input:
Options:
A. Paleoindians inhabited a wide diversity of habitats, including some of the highest elevations in the New World.
B. Paleoindians were primarily adapted to coastal regions and interior grassland habitats, where they could hunt large mammals.
C. Paleoindians used the best quality obsidian to make microblades and fluted points for hunting large mammals.
D. Paleoindians followed a coastal migratory route to enter the New World and spread across South America, where they lived mostly in rockshelters and caves.
output: A. Paleoindians inhabited a wide diversity of habitats, including some of the highest elevations in the New World.

instruction: Some argue that Homo erectus in fact comprised several related but geographically distinct species. If so, this includes which of the following?
input:
Options:
A. Homo ergaster in Asia, Homo erectus in Europe, Homo antecessor in Africa
B. Homo ergaster in Europe, Homo erectus in Africa, Homo antecessor in Asia
C. Homo ergaster in Africa, Homo erectus in Asia, Homo antecessor in Europe
D. Homo ergaster in Europe, Homo erectus in Africa and Asia, Homo antecessor in Australia
output: C. Homo ergaster in Africa, Homo erectus in Asia, Homo antecessor in Europe

instruction: When did maize-based agriculture replace the traditional foraging subsistence system in the Southwest?
input:
Options:
A. 500 B.P.
B. 1000 B.P.
C. 2000 B.P.
D. 3000 B.P.

instruction: Genetic analysis shows that humans and chimps have been evolving separately for about how long?
input:
Options:
A. 2 million years
B. 4 million years
C. 7 million years
D. 15 million years
output: C. 7 million years

instruction: Which of the following signifies that a person was very young when they died?
input:
Options:
A. the fusion of the epiphyses to the diaphysis
B. the absence of cranial sutures
C. the presence of deciduous dentition
D. all of the above
output: C. the presence of deciduous dentition

instruction: Human domination of the planet is a culmination of:
input:
Options:
A. the development of sophisticated tools, controlled use of fire, working cooperatively, and reliance on intelligence.
B. evolution of a larger body, increased strength, hunting, and increased warfare.
C. bipedalism, working independently, increased violence, and survival of the fittest.
D. all of the above.
output: A. the development of sophisticated tools, controlled use of fire, working cooperatively, and reliance on intelligence.

instruction: Agriculture allows for complexity because:
input:
Options:
A. people end up consuming more protein.
B. children begin working and contributing at an earlier age.
C. it only takes a few people to feed many, therefore freeing up enormous labor potential.
D. vegetables contain vitamins not available in meat or fish.
output: C. it only takes a few people to feed many, therefore freeing up enormous labor potential.

instruction: What was the climate of Greater Australia 20,000 years ago?
input:
Options:
A. temperate
B. hot and dry
C. frozen tundra
D. all the above
output: D. all the above

instruction: The mean size of a Homo habilis brain is roughly:
input:
Options:
A. 300 cc.
B. 450 cc.
C. 700 cc.
D. 1200 cc.

instruction: Which of the following best describes an archaeologist's perspective of culture?
input:
Options:
A. a common language shared by one group of people for survival
B. a genetically-determined adaptation that allows certain kinds of artifacts and technology to be replicated
C. learned and invented adaptations or strategies for survival which are not genetically determined
D. artifacts and artwork that inspire people and improve the average person's quality of life
output: C. learned and invented adaptations or strategies for survival which are not genetically determined

instruction: Which structures housed religious ceremonies?
input:
Options:
A. pit-houses
B. pueblos
C. kivas
D. courtyard groups
output: C. kivas

instruction: Which of the following appears to be a hybridization of Neandertal and modern human stone tool technologies?
input:
Options:
A. Châtelperronian
B. Levallois
C. Aurignacian
D. Mousterian
output: A. Châtelperronian

instruction: The ridge of bone that runs along the top of the skull in Australopithecus robustus is called a:
input:
Options:
A. diastema.
B. cranium.
C. maxilla.
D. sagittal crest.
output: D. sagittal crest.

instruction: When Hernan Cortes entered the Aztec city of Tenochtitlán in A.D. __________, its population was estimated to be _____________.
What were the mastaba?
input:
Options:
A. clay tablets that represent the earliest known form of writing in the world
B. mud-brick structures built over elite tombs that were subsequently developed into pyramids
C. irrigation canals that allowed for the production of agricultural surpluses in Egypt
D. the ritual headdress of the religious-political leaders of Mesopotamia
output: B. mud-brick structures built over elite tombs that were subsequently developed into pyramids

instruction: Lewis Henry Morgan's stages of human culture are known as:
input:
Options:
A. Three-Age system.
B. Natural selection.
C. Multilineal evolution.
D. Unilineal evolution.
output: D. Unilineal evolution.

instruction: A state society is:
input:
Options:
A. characterized by social inequality and the absence of hunting.
B. a stratified society whose rulers have the powers to tax, make laws, and conscript labor.
C. a system in which all members of the same age and sex category possess equal wealth and standing.
D. a political organization with no central leader whose subunits make collective decisions.
output: B. a stratified society whose rulers have the powers to tax, make laws, and conscript labor.

instruction: The village of Snaketown covers more than one square mile and had a well-developed irrigation network and evidence of a ceremonial ballgame. It was the largest village of which complex society?
input:
Options:
A. Ancestral Puebloan
B. Hohokam
C. Mississippian
D. Adena
output: C. Mississippian

instruction: Analysis of the Denisovan, Neanderthals, and modern human genomes suggests that:
input:
Options:
A. Neandertals and Denisovans diverged from a common population of premodern humans.
B. Neandertals and Denisovans are more similar to one another than either is to anatomically modern humans.
C. Neandertals and modern humans are more similar to one another than either is to Denisovans.
D. both a and b.
output: D. both a and b.

instruction: Since the late 1800s, tidal gauges indicate that mean global sea level has ________; there is consensus among scientists that sea level ______.
input:
Options:
A. decreased by about 5 centimeters (2 inches); will soon begin to rise.
B. remained constant; may begin to rise if glaciers melt.
C. increased by about 5 centimeters (2 inches); will continue to rise.
D. increased by about 20 centimeters (8 inches); will continue to rise.
output: D. increased by about 20 centimeters (8 inches); will continue to rise.

instruction: The Bering Strait was above water, on and off, between
The idea that processes like weathering and erosion are responsible for the present condition of the earth is known as:
input:
Options:
A. uniformitarianism.
B. natural selection.
C. creationism.
D. adaptation.
output: A. uniformitarianism.

instruction: Who was part of the elite class in the Olmec culture?
input:
Options:
A. those who lived in the particularly rich farmlands
B. those who lived near resource-privileged areas
C. those who lived near the river where trading took place
D. those who lived near the volcanic rocks used in tool making
output: B. those who lived near resource-privileged areas

instruction: The earthen monument called Mound 72 contained the burials of more than 270 people, including an adult male interred on a platform with 20,000 conch-shell beads in the shape of a giant bird. Mound 72 represents the most complex ______ society at ________.
input:
Options:
A. Ancestral Puebloan; Pueblo Bonito
B. Hohokam; Casa Grande
C. Mississippian; Cahokia
D. Adena; Snaketown.
output: C. Mississippian; Cahokia

instruction: Which sites have provided evidence used in arguing against the hypothesis that social complexity always required the production of agricultural surpluses?
input:
Options:
A. Stonehenge and Caral
B. Catalhoyuk and Gobekli Tepe
C. La Venta and Catalhoyuk
D. Gobekli Tepe and Poverty Point
output: D. Gobekli Tepe and Poverty Point

instruction: What best characterizes the subsistence strategies of the North American Archaic period?
input:
Options:
A. increased reliance on farming
B. decreased reliance on shellfish
C. greater regional differentiation
D. active trading between the North and South
output: C. greater regional differentiation

instruction: Identify the correct sequence of mean cranial capacities for premodern Homo sapiens, Neandertals, and modern Homo sapiens.
Genetic evidence from the oldest known human skeletons in the New World dating from no more than __________ years ago indicate close connections between _________.
input:
Options:
A. 23,000; the skeletal remains of the first Americans, Native Americans, and the ancient and modern inhabitants of western Europe.
B. 13,000; the skeletal remains of the first Americans, Native Americans, and the ancient and modern inhabitants of Siberia.
C. 8,000; the skeletal remains of the first Americans, Austral-Melanesians, and the ancient and modern inhabitants of Melanesia.
D. 6,000; the skeletal remains of the first Americans, Clovis culture, and the ancient and modern inhabitants of the Arctic.
output: B. 13,000; the skeletal remains of the first Americans, Native Americans, and the ancient and modern inhabitants of Siberia.

instruction: Capacocha was an Incan ritual that involved what?
input:
Options:
A. drinking maize beer and feasting on the hearts of slain enemies
B. sacrificing virgins in order to appease the serpent god
C. sacrificing captives of war in order to propitiate the sun god
D. sacrificing children in order to propitiate the spirits of the mountains
output: D. sacrificing children in order to propitiate the spirits of the mountains

instruction: Which of the following was NOT a factor in the extinction of the Neandertals?
input:
Options:
A. They were specialized for an environment that suddenly changed.
B. Their tool technology was less advanced.
C. They were unsuited to the hotter climates of the sub-Saharan savanna.
D. The Neandertal body type required greater amounts of calories to sustain.
output: C. They were unsuited to the hotter climates of the sub-Saharan savanna.

instruction: A preserved pile of trash, often containing food remains, is called a _____________. At the Danish site of Meilgaard, one of these places contained millions of ______________.
input:
Options:
A. midden; mollusk shells
B. camelid; pottery sherds
C. rachis; bones of domesticated cattle.
D. littoral; microblades
output: A. midden; mollusk shells

instruction: Unlike most other early civilizations, Minoan culture shows little evidence of:
input:
Options:
A. trade.
B. warfare.
C. the development of a common religion.
D. conspicuous consumption by elites.
output: D. conspicuous consumption by elites.

instruction: The greatest Egyptian pyramids at Giza were built:
input:
Options:
A. as burial monuments for the pharaoh Khufu, Khufu's son Khafre, and Khufu's grandson Menkaure.
B. by slaves who were coerced and worked under the threat of death, as described in the book of Exodus of the Old Testament.
C. in the construction frenzy of the 6th dynasty.
D. all of the above.
output: A. as burial monuments for the pharaoh Khufu, Khufu's son Khafre, and Khufu's grandson Menkaure.

instruction: When anatomically modern humans first arrived in the Middle East, who did they encounter?
input:
Options:
A. Neandertals, the evolutionary descendants of the premodern human inhabitants of Europe and Asia
B. Homo erectus, the evolutionary descendants of the premodern human inhabitants of Europe and Asia
C. Homo sapiens, who had evolved independently in Asia and arrived there by 200,000 years ago
D. All of the above
output: A. Neandertals, the evolutionary descendants of the premodern human inhabitants of Europe and Asia

instruction: The “Lion Man” from Hohlenstein-Stadel cave is an example of:
input:
Options:
A. mobiliary art.
B. long-distance trade of exotic raw materials.
C. parietal art.
D. a Venus figurine.
output: A. mobiliary art.

instruction: At its peak, the palace at Knossos is thought to have had over _________ rooms.
The Hopewell were complex rank societies, but they were not a state. Hopewell culture lacked all of the following elements EXCEPT:
input:
Options:
A. formal government
B. monumental earthworks
C. urban centers
D. a permanent military
output: B. monumental earthworks

instruction: Markings found on the mud-bricks of Huaca del Sol are probably:
input:
Options:
A. instructions for the builders written there by the engineers.
B. random scratches and not a meaningful script or written language.
C. intended to identify the local group that had produced them.
D. simple arithmetic performed by carpenters on the building site.
output: C. intended to identify the local group that had produced them.

instruction: The 30 upright stones at Stonehenge are called _______; the horizontal stones are _________.
input:
Options:
A. legumes, sarsens
B. lintels, stelae
C. sarsens, lintels
D. trilithon, tholoi
output: C. sarsens, lintels

instruction: The secondarily altricial condition of modern human babies may have been an evolutionary solution, in that:
input:
Options:
A. the brain size of hominids had not grown for more than a million years, making it difficult for babies to walk.
B. it allowed for bipedalism and independence from the mother at an earlier age.
C. it allowed for subsequent growth of the brain, since bipedalism had resulted in a narrowed birth canal in the female pelvis.
D. it allowed for growth of the brain to nearly adult size prior to birth, since bipedalism had resulted in a wider birth canal in the female pelvis.
output: C. it allowed for subsequent growth of the brain, since bipedalism had resulted in a narrowed birth canal in the female pelvis.

instruction: Research on C3 and C4 pathways indicates that changes in plant communities were associated with a transition in the diets of ancient hominids from:
input:
Options:
A. species focused on grasses to nuts and fruits.
B. meat to fruits and vegetables.
C. fruits and vegetables to fish.
D. nuts and fruits to species more focused on grasses.
output: D. nuts and fruits to species more focused on grasses.

instruction: Which of the following is evidence of new uses for plants during the Middle Stone Age?
input:
Options:
A. the use of seeds as a natural insecticide in Altamira cave in southwestern Europe
B. plant materials such as flowers in Aurignacian burials in southern France
C. plant material lining the floor of Sibudu Cave in South Africa
D. the use of wood in the Gravettian tradition to make spear-throwers and canoes
output: C. plant material lining the floor of Sibudu Cave in South Africa

instruction: That modern Africans do not possess any Neandertal DNA indicates that:
input:
Options:
A. Gene flow between Neandertals and anatomically modern humans must have occurred before Neandertals migrated out of Africa.
B. Gene flow between Neandertals and anatomically modern humans occurred after anatomically modern humans migrated out of Africa.
C. Neandertals who lived in Africa did not interbreed with anatomically modern humans, but must have followed them when they migrated out of Africa.
D. Interbreeding between anatomically modern humans and Neandertals never occurred.
output: B. Gene flow between Neandertals and anatomically modern humans occurred after anatomically modern humans migrated out of Africa.

instruction: Toward the end of the Pleistocene, between 28,000 and 18,000 years ago, worldwide sea level was much lower than present day, resulting in the exposure of a landmass east of Siberia called __________. This period is called the _______.
input:
Options:
A. Beringia; Late Beringian Period
B. Sundaland; McKenzie Maximum
C. Beringia; Late Glacial Maximum
D. Wallacea; Late Laurentide Period
output: C. Beringia; Late Glacial Maximum

instruction: Which archaeological method is best for identifying large-scale land modifications?
input:
Options:
A. test pits
B. ground-penetrating radar
C. aerial photography
D. proton magnetometers
output: C. aerial photography

instruction: What designation for a pottery style was eventually applied to an entire cultural complex that moved across the Pacific?
input:
Options:
A. Clovis
B. Nenana Complex
C. Lapita
D. Micronesian Pottery Tradition
output: C. Lapita

instruction: What is one of the differences between simple foragers and complex foragers?
input:
Options:
A. Complex foragers employ irrigation technology.
B. Complex foragers rely on a wider range of food sources.
C. Complex foragers are more highly mobile.
D. Complex foragers focus on a few highly productive resources.
output: D. Complex foragers focus on a few highly productive resources.

instruction: The significance of Frere's discovery was that what he found was located:
input:
Options:
A. beneath the remains of extinct animals.
B. on the surface, above the remains of extinct animals.
C. in a region of Africa where no one thought humans had ever lived.
D. on top of the ruins of a Medieval castle.
output: A. beneath the remains of extinct animals.

instruction: What is the earliest form of writing in the world and where did it develop?
input:
Options:
A. cuneiform, in Mesopotamia
B. hieroglyphics, in Egypt
C. clay-tablets, at Knossos
D. runes, at Stonehenge
output: A. cuneiform, in Mesopotamia

instruction: A pattern of social integration in which individuals are placed into a hierarchy of social levels is called:
input:
Options:
A. urbanization.
B. a social system.
C. social stratification.
D. a necropolis.
output: C. social stratification.

instruction: The Minoan economy may have been especially vulnerable to natural catastrophe because it relied heavily on:
input:
Options:
A. agriculture
B. maritime trade
C. metalworking
D. slave labor
output: B. maritime trade

instruction: The _______ developed one of the earliest kingdoms in South America, reaching its height at around _________.
input:
Options:
A. Moche; AD 400
B. Wari; AD 100
C. Inca; AD 200
D. Maya; AD 400
output: A. Moche; AD 400

instruction: What is the name of the lithic technology seen in the Arctic and consisting of wedge-shaped cores, micro-blades, bifacial knives, and burins?
input:
Options:
A. Clovis Complex
B. Denali Complex
C. Folsom Complex
D. Nenana Complex
output: B. Denali Complex

instruction: Which of the following is used to remove the soil enclosing site materials?
input:
Options:
A. brushes
B. trowels
C. dental picks
D. all of the above
output: D. all of the above

instruction: A continuous, projecting ridge of bone above and across the eye orbits is called the:
input:
Options:
A. sagittal crest.
B. supraorbital torus.
C. maxilla.
D. occipital bone.
output: B. supraorbital torus.

instruction: Ancestral Puebloan culture in Chaco Canyon was comprised of:
input:
Options:
A. around 75 substantial settlements and more than 300 smaller communities.
B. more than 500 towns and villages with monumental architecture.
C. between 30 and 40 farmsteads and three large pueblos.
D. one large city state with more than 300 outlying farmsteads.
output: A. around 75 substantial settlements and more than 300 smaller communities.

instruction: The Yang-shao culture gave way to the Lung-Shan sometime after:
The most prominent feature of the food resource base of post-Pleistocene Europe was its:
input:
Options:
A. dependence on megafauna.
B. hunting and gathering.
C. dependence on fur-bearing animals.
D. diversity.
output: D. diversity.

instruction: Evidence of wild grain harvesting and consumption in Israel dates to as early as
Civilization in the Indus Valley was characterized by:
input:
Options:
A. highly centralized economies.
B. carefully planned and designed cities.
C. standardized weights and measures.
D. all of the above.
output: D. all of the above.

instruction: According to one theory, the power of Ancestral Pueblo elites emerged when certain groups:
input:
Options:
A. predicted astronomical events such as eclipses and meteor showers.
B. constructed monuments and elaborate multi-storied cliff dwellings.
C. stored food surpluses in good years for distribution in bad years.
D. incorporated other societies through conquest warfare.
output: C. stored food surpluses in good years for distribution in bad years.

instruction: Teotihuacán came to prominence in the Basin of Mexico after its rival, Cuicuilco,
input:
Options:
A. was crippled by a volcanic eruption.
B. succumbed to a civil war among its ruling families.
C. suffered a blight on its crops.
D. was flooded by a Gulf Coast hurricane.
output: A. was crippled by a volcanic eruption.

instruction: Evidence from northwest coast societies indicates that what is ultimately needed for the development of social complexity is:
input:
Options:
A. agriculture.
B. irrigation technology.
C. social stratification.
D. a food surplus.
output: D. a food surplus.

instruction: Which subfield of anthropology aims to better understand the nearest living relatives of humans?
input:
Options:
A. paleoanthropology
B. archaeology
C. primatology
D. linguistics
output: C. primatology

instruction: How did Aurignacian technology differ from Mousterian technology?
input:
Options:
A. Mousterian technology produced more projectile points.
B. Mousterian technology produced more usable blade surface.
C. Aurignacian technology produced more usable blade surface.
D. Aurignacian technology was focused on the production of hand axes.
output: C. Aurignacian technology produced more usable blade surface.

instruction: Which of the following is evidence of a complex society?
input:
Options:
A. monumental works
B. burials with grave goods
C. leisure and a sedentary lifestyle
D. all of the above
output: A. monumental works

instruction: The face of Homo erectus was more ________ than modern humans, but less so than Homo habilis.
input:
Options:
A. altricial
B. hairy
C. occipital
D. prognathous
output: D. prognathous

instruction: Montezuma ruled over millions of people from the _______ capital of _____.
input:
Options:
A. Maya; Tikal.
B. Aztec; Tenochtitlán.
C. Teotihuacános; Teotihuacán.
D. Zapotec; Monte Albán.
output: B. Aztec; Tenochtitlán.

instruction: The belief that all of the characteristics of civilization developed in one place, such as Egypt, and from there spread out to the rest of the world is known as:
input:
Options:
A. cultural evolution
B. migrationism
C. diffusionism
D. anti-originalism
output: C. diffusionism

instruction: When the ratio of brain size to body size is compared, which species has a proportionally larger brain?
input:
Options:
A. Homo erectus
B. premodern Homo sapiens
C. Neandertals
D. modern Homo sapiens
output: D. modern Homo sapiens

instruction: The royal graves of the Shang Dynasty consisted of enormous cruciform-shaped tombs, where the deceased kings were buried with:
input:
Options:
A. jade, bronze, and ceramic artifacts.
B. chariots and horses.
C. the headless bodies of humans who had been sacrificed.
D. all of the above.
output: D. all of the above.

instruction: The above hominid species discovered in Malapa Cave in South Africa has been classified as:
input:
Options:
A. Homo habilis
B. Australopithecus sediba.
C. Homo sapiens.
D. Australopithecus robustus
output: B. Australopithecus sediba.

instruction: Ethnographic evidence supports which of the following connections between surplus food and social complexity?
input:
Options:
A. Only agriculturalists can produce the food surplus necessary for economic inequality.
B. Some resource-rich environments allow for the creation of surpluses that can lead to economic inequalities and social complexity.
C. Economic inequalities are the foundation of social complexity and entirely dependent on agriculture for the production of surplus food.
D. The production of surplus food is not important in the development of economic inequalities or social complexity.
output: B. Some resource-rich environments allow for the creation of surpluses that can lead to economic inequalities and social complexity.

instruction: Which of the following was the greatest advantage of using fire in human evolution?
input:
Options:
A. Fire offers protection from predators and enemies.
B. Fire makes meat more digestible and kills bacteria.
C. Fire produces light and heat.
D. Fire can be used in warfare and to clear fields.
output: B. Fire makes meat more digestible and kills bacteria.

instruction: Palynology is the study of _________, which allows scientists to reconstruct ______.
input:
Options:
A. foraminifera; a master sequence of tree rings.
B. coprolites; paleopathology and sexual dimorphism.
C. pollen; plant communities and climate.
D. phytoliths; artificial selection and photosynthesis pathways.
output: C. pollen; plant communities and climate.

instruction: What was the unifying element of Olmec culture?
input:
Options:
A. religious iconography
B. large armies
C. agricultural surpluses
D. all of the above
output: A. religious iconography

instruction: Which of the following ancient civilizations has a written language that is the furthest from being fully deciphered?
input:
Options:
A. the Indus Valley
B. Egyptian
C. Mesopotamian
D. Chinese
output: A. the Indus Valley

instruction: The sophisticated stone tool making industry at the Pinnacle Point site in South Africa is evidence of:
input:
Options:
A. a 250,000-year-old tradition of hand axe production and use.
B. a 71,000-year-old complex sequence of microblade production and use.
C. an adaptation to hunting in colder environments.
D. both a and c.
output: B. a 71,000-year-old complex sequence of microblade production and use.

instruction: Early evidence of complexity in Mayan societies is suggested by the appearance, around 2650 B.P., of:
input:
Options:
A. finely carved obsidian statuary.
B. decorated stepped platforms.
C. the introduction of chocolate into the Mesoamerican economy.
D. a ritual ball game in which the losers were sacrificed to the gods.
output: B. decorated stepped platforms.

instruction: What do anthropologists NOT need to know to determine when people entered the Americas from Siberia?
input:
Options:
A. When sled dogs were first domesticated
B. When the Bering Strait was exposed and open for travel
C. When eastern Siberia was first inhabited
D. The age of the earliest New World sites
output: A. When sled dogs were first domesticated

instruction: When did Aborigines occupy the harsh interior of Australia?
input:
Options:
A. 10,000–12,000 years ago
B. 20,000–25,000 years ago
C. 35,000–40,000 years ago
D. 40,000–45,000 years ago

instruction: What do the Hassunan and Samarran sites in Mesopotamia have in common?
input:
Options:
A. Both relied heavily on agriculture.
B. Both have an abundance of rare luxury items.
C. Both have high-status burials.
D. Both have sophisticated monumental architecture.
output: A. Both relied heavily on agriculture.

instruction: Which crop is South America's most significant agricultural contribution to Europe?
input:
Options:
A. rice
B. potatoes
C. squash
D. beans
output: B. potatoes

instruction: What distinguishes the trade patterns of the Mesolithic from those of the Upper Paleolithic?
input:
Options:
A. in the Mesolithic, goods traveled farther and more goods were exchanged
B. in the Mesolithic, goods traveled farther but fewer goods were exchanged
C. in the Mesolithic, goods traveled less far but more goods were exchanged
D. in the Mesolithic, goods traveled less far and fewer goods were exchanged
output: C. in the Mesolithic, goods traveled less far but more goods were exchanged

instruction: A celebration in which wealth is redistributed is called a:
input:
Options:
A. potlatch.
B. kiva parties.
C. totem feasts.
D. sinagua.
output: A. potlatch.

instruction: Which of the following are techniques of trace element analysis?
input:
Options:
A. proton magnetometer and electrical resistivity
B. accelerator mass spectrometry and photosynthesis pathways
C. carbon isotope analysis and experimental replication
D. neutron activation analysis and X- ray fluorescence
output: D. neutron activation analysis and X- ray fluorescence

instruction: The Chinese process of divining the future by examining fired animal bones is called:
input:
Options:
A. hang-t'u.
B. sarsen divination
C. scapulimancy
D. cylinder seal prophecy
output: C. scapulimancy

instruction: How have archaeologists characterized the monuments built by the Olmec?
input:
Options:
A. Halafian ritual monuments
B. megalithic chiefdoms
C. surplus food storage centers
D. regal-ritual centers
output: D. regal-ritual centers

instruction: The ethics of conducting archaeological research on sites with human remains of indigenous North American ancestors is addressed by the Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act. Problems often arise when:
input:
Options:
A. both non-indigenous archaeologists and Native Americans are allowed onto the site at the same time.
B. there are no Native Americans who have been trained as archaeologists and no archaeologists who are Native American.
C. neither archaeologists nor Native Americans can agree on the exact location of burials at the site.
D. burials are so ancient that establishing historical or genealogical connections with modern, living groups of people is impossible.
output: D. burials are so ancient that establishing historical or genealogical connections with modern, living groups of people is impossible.

instruction: Which culture, previously-known as the temple-mound builders, based their subsistence primarily on maize and squash agriculture?
input:
Options:
A. Ancestral Puebloan
B. Hohokam
C. Mississippian
D. Adena
output: C. Mississippian

instruction: The city of Uruk and the cultures of the Maya and the Moche were all adversely affected by:
input:
Options:
A. invasion.
B. drought.
C. civil war.
D. earthquakes.
output: B. drought.

instruction: What is the wild progenitor of maize?
input:
Options:
A. einkorn
B. emmer
C. teosinte
D. legumes
output: C. teosinte

instruction: In comparison to the Middle Paleolithic, Upper Paleolithic tool technologies:
input:
Options:
A. emphasized flakes over blades.
B. changed rapidly.
C. involved elaborate preparation of core tools.
D. all of the above
output: B. changed rapidly.

instruction: Recent genomic analyses of Neandertals and modern human populations indicate that:
input:
Options:
A. between 1% and 4% of the genome of modern humans with European and Asian ancestry originated from Neandertal populations, most likely through interbreeding.
B. Neandertal populations were entirely distinct and separate from anatomically modern humans, with no evidence of interbreeding.
C. anatomically modern humans throughout the world uniformly share approximately 16% of their genome with Neandertal populations.
D. modern Africans share more than 4% of their genome with Neandertals, far greater than modern European and Asian populations, indicating a lengthier time of successful interbreeding.
output: A. between 1% and 4% of the genome of modern humans with European and Asian ancestry originated from Neandertal populations, most likely through interbreeding.

instruction: Which of the following is a remote-sensing device used at archaeological sites?
input:
Options:
A. ground-penetrating radar
B. proton magnetometer
C. electrical resistivity
D. all the above
output: D. all the above

instruction: Genetic studies of the two primary varieties of rice, japonica (short-grained), and indica (long-grained), suggest that:
input:
Options:
A. each is more closely related to one another than their local wild ancestors, suggesting that these modern varieties of rice were developed recently in east Asia.
B. each is more closely related to local wild ancestors than one another, suggesting that these modern varieties of rice were domesticated separately in east Asia and south Asia.
C. each is unrelated to one another, suggesting that these modern varieties of rice were domesticated independently in east Asia and western Europe.
D. each is closely related to their local wild ancestors, suggesting that domestication must have occurred very recently and no earlier than 2,000 years ago.
output: B. each is more closely related to local wild ancestors than one another, suggesting that these modern varieties of rice were domesticated separately in east Asia and south Asia.

instruction: What do the amount of grave goods buried with the children at Sungir' indicate?
input:
Options:
A. The tribe spent most of their time carving beads.
B. The tribe was involved in an intricate trade network.
C. The tribe had a complex system of inherited social statuses.
D. The children were sometimes leaders of the tribe.
output: C. The tribe had a complex system of inherited social statuses.

instruction: At its peak, the population of the city of Teotihuacán may have reached:
input:
Options:
A. 50,000 people.
B. 200,000 people.
C. 500,000 people.
D. 1,000,000 people.
output: B. 200,000 people.

instruction: Nubian civilization:
input:
Options:
A. predated and spurred the rise of Egyptian culture.
B. was the result of Mesopotamian colonization in the south.
C. developed in response to, but not in imitation of, Egyptian culture.
D. had no contacts with neighboring cultures.
output: C. developed in response to, but not in imitation of, Egyptian culture.

instruction: Having a forward-thrusting lower face is called
input:
Options:
A. arboreal.
B. prognathous.
C. diastema.
D. mandible.
output: B. prognathous.

instruction: What may have caused the Ancestral Puebloans to abandon Mesa Verde?
input:
Options:
A. the population outstripped the productive capacity of the environment
B. drought
C. a new religion attracted them to the south
D. all of the above
output: D. all of the above

instruction: Which species is most typically first associated with the fashioning and use of stone tools?
input:
Options:
A. Homo habilis
B. Ardipithecus ramidus
C. Homo sapiens
D. Australopithecus robustus
output: A. Homo habilis

instruction: A design that is not painted upon but is etched into a rock face is called a:
input:
Options:
A. pictograph.
B. petroglyph.
C. pictorial.
D. petrification.
output: B. petroglyph.

instruction: The Gault site in south-central Texas has produced evidence from 13,000 years ago that Paleoindians chose this location based on the:
input:
Options:
A. nearness of the site to navigable rivers and the Gulf coast.
B. abundance of wild game, plants, and fish in a rich and diverse woodland environment.
C. proximity to a local source of chert for quarrying and making stone tools.
D. nearby location of migratory routes of large mammals such as bison.
output: C. proximity to a local source of chert for quarrying and making stone tools.

instruction: The early Mesolithic Maglemosian culture was adapted to:
input:
Options:
A. a tundra environment.
B. a desert environment.
C. a forest and lakeside environment.
D. an equatorial environment.
output: C. a forest and lakeside environment.

instruction: How were the first metals worked in South America?
input:
Options:
A. casting
B. hammering
C. smelting
D. all of the above
output: B. hammering

instruction: What is the Aztec word for a spear-throwing device developed in Europe more than 30,000 years ago?
input:
Options:
A. chunkey.
B. atlatl.
C. burin.
D. petroglyph.
output: B. atlatl.

instruction: The directed breeding of plants and animals by humans is called:
input:
Options:
A. foraging.
B. artificial selection.
C. natural selection.
D. herding.
output: B. artificial selection.

instruction: Interestingly, none of the civilizations of ancient South America appear to have developed:
input:
Options:
A. monumental works.
B. irrigation technology.
C. a written language.
D. significant armies.
output: C. a written language.

instruction: Which of the following is not a hypothesis for why hominids walked on two legs?
input:
Options:
A. it freed the hands to carry things
B. it allowed for braincase expansion
C. it expended less energy than quadrupedalism for going long distances
D. it allowed hominids to see greater distances
output: B. it allowed for braincase expansion

instruction: When did the first pharaohs emerge in Egypt?
There is evidence that the Hohokam borrowed which practice from Mesoamerican culture?
input:
Options:
A. ritual consumption of maize beer
B. ritual human sacrifice
C. playing ritual ball games
D. construction of stepped pyramids
output: C. playing ritual ball games

instruction: One of the less obvious reasons for the Inca to fight so many wars may have been:
input:
Options:
A. to develop a story line for powerful epic poetry.
B. to identify and cultivate talented leaders.
C. to kill off a certain percentage of the young male population, thus preventing revolution.
D. to appease the gods of war.
output: B. to identify and cultivate talented leaders.

instruction: The name Teotihuacán was given to the city by:
input:
Options:
A. the Aztecs, who continued to make pilgrimages there long after its collapse.
B. the Spanish invaders, who largely destroyed it.
C. the city's first king, who named it after his favorite deity.
D. Olmec traders, who were impressed with its grandeur.
output: A. the Aztecs, who continued to make pilgrimages there long after its collapse.

instruction: Which culture hosted the above celebration?
input:
Options:
A. the Ancestral Puebloans of the southwestern desert
B. the Mogollon of the southwestern mountains
C. the Kwakiutl of the Pacific Northwest
D. the Hopewell of the American Midwest
output: C. the Kwakiutl of the Pacific Northwest

instruction: Of the following, which is the earliest example of the development of a complex society?
input:
Options:
A. Jericho in Israel
B. Caral in Peru
C. Stonehenge in England
D. Olmec along the Gulf Coast
output: A. Jericho in Israel

instruction: Archaeological evidence for the domestication of cats suggests it occurred when and why?
input:
Options:
A. before 22,000 years ago, as a result of the shift from opportunistic foraging to logistical collecting
B. before 11,000 years ago, as a direct result of artificial selection
C. after 11,000 years ago, as an unintentional consequence of food production and storage
D. after 9,000 years ago, as an unintentional result of the domestication of cattle and production of milk and cheese
output: C. after 11,000 years ago, as an unintentional consequence of food production and storage

instruction: The most obvious material symbols of ancient state societies are:
input:
Options:
A. stone tablets.
B. pyramids.
C. monumental works.
D. irrigation canals.
output: C. monumental works.

instruction: What is the evidence for trade between Indus Valley cities and the city states of ancient Mesopotamia?
input:
Options:
A. Obsidian tools have been found at sites in both regions.
B. Glass beads, copper, and gold from Mesopotamia have been found at Harappan sites in the Indus Valley.
C. Harappan seals have been found in Mesopotamia and Mesopotamian cylinder seals have been found in the Indus valley.
D. All of the above.
output: C. Harappan seals have been found in Mesopotamia and Mesopotamian cylinder seals have been found in the Indus valley.

instruction: At the end of the Miocene many species of ape became extinct due to:
input:
Options:
A. humans killing them.
B. an asteroid hitting the Yucatan Peninsula.
C. a change in the environment.
D. dinosaurs eating them.
output: C. a change in the environment.

instruction: Some of the oldest painted art in the world was recently discovered in caves on the island of Sulawesi in Indonesia. What do the images include and to when do they date?
input:
Options:
A. animals and human bodies from more than 15,000 to about 20,000 years ago
B. animals and hand stencils from more than 35,000 to about 40,000 years ago
C. animals and hand stencils from more than 45,000 to about 100,000 years ago
D. animals and abstract geometric shapes from 15,000 to more than 100,000 years ago
output: B. animals and hand stencils from more than 35,000 to about 40,000 years ago

instruction: A person who believes that the current appearance of the earth can be best explained as having resulted from a series of natural disasters is known as a(n):
input:
Options:
A. paleoanthropologist.
B. natural scientist.
C. evolutionist.
D. catastrophist.
output: D. catastrophist.

instruction: What contributes to societies becoming more complex?
input:
Options:
A. Surplus food is stored in large, collective facilities.
B. Crop irrigation requires the construction of dams or canals.
C. Sedentary communities need to defend themselves.
D. All of the above.
output: D. All of the above.

instruction: A(n) _________ contains primary refuse; a _________ contains secondary refuse.
input:
Options:
A. kitchen; garden
B. activity area; burial
C. picnic site; trash dump
D. activity area; recycling area
output: C. picnic site; trash dump

instruction: Artifacts _________; ecofacts __________
input:
Options:
A. are valuable and rare; are easy to come by.
B. decay rapidly; last for a long time.
C. are made by humans; exhibit traces of human activity.
D. are facts about art; are facts about nature.
output: C. are made by humans; exhibit traces of human activity.

instruction: Pompeii was unusually well preserved because:
input:
Options:
A. the layer of volcanic pumice created a seal over the remains.
B. avalanches pushed the remains into the sea and seawater preserves things.
C. poisonous volcanic gases killed people instantly.
D. the Romans embalmed the victims with salt from seawater.
output: A. the layer of volcanic pumice created a seal over the remains.

instruction: Charles Lyell argued that the Earth must be extremely old based on the fact that:
input:
Options:
A. many processes that can be observed act extremely slowly.
B. uniformitarianism can account for significant geological features.
C. erosion works incredibly slowly.
D. All of the above.
output: D. All of the above.

instruction: Homo floresiensis from the island of Flores dates from around 35,000 to 14,000 years ago, and according to some researchers, is similar or related to:
input:
Options:
A. Homo erectus.
B. Homo habilis.
C. Homo ergaster.
D. Australopithecus afarensis.
output: A. Homo erectus.

instruction: Subsistence practices of people can be determined by recovering and studying:
input:
Options:
A. the faunal assemblage from a site.
B. an osteological comparative collection from a site.
C. pumice and evidence of pyroclastic surges.
D. all of the above.
output: A. the faunal assemblage from a site.

instruction: When the Spanish explorer Hernando de Soto crossed a portion of the North American continent, his expedition encountered direct descendants of which people?
input:
Options:
A. Mississippian
B. Adena
C. Ancestral Puebloan
D. Kwakiutl
output: A. Mississippian

instruction: Following the classical period, which ended around A.D. 800, Mayan civilization:
input:
Options:
A. inexplicably disappeared, then began a slow development ending with Aztec civilization.
B. entered the second classical period, lost a great war with Teotihuacán, and faded away.
C. fell into decline, moved its center north, resurged, and fell into decline once again.
D. fell into a sudden decline; the population disappeared and never again built monumental structures.
output: C. fell into decline, moved its center north, resurged, and fell into decline once again.

instruction: During the late Miocene, carbon isotope analysis indicates environmental changes that would have impacted the hominid ancestors of modern humans. These changes are best characterized as:
input:
Options:
A. a sudden drop in global temperatures resulting in a return to ice age conditions.
B. a sudden rise in global temperatures resulting in rising sea levels.
C. an expansion of grasslands and reduction in woodlands, resulting in regional mosaic environments.
D. a decline in large mammal populations and relative increase in other classes of vertebrate species.
output: C. an expansion of grasslands and reduction in woodlands, resulting in regional mosaic environments.

instruction: Which of the following characteristics of modern humans is the most ancient, pre-dating the Late Stone Age, the Upper Paleolithic and even anatomically modern humans?
input:
Options:
A. elaborate burials
B. larger sites with larger populations
C. improved stone tool technologies
D. symbolic expression through the production of art
output: C. improved stone tool technologies

instruction: Moving through trees by swinging arm over arm is called:
input:
Options:
A. bipedal locomotion.
B. brachiation.
C. quadrupedal locomotion.
D. a savanna niche.
output: B. brachiation.

instruction: Why is Catalhoyuk in central Turkey regarded as a large village but not a city?
input:
Options:
A. There were no palaces, public architecture, and little evidence for status differentiation.
B. There was no evidence for food storage, domesticated animals, or buildings.
C. There were no works of art, rituals, or activities associated with cities.
D. There was no evidence for monumental architecture or roads.
output: A. There were no palaces, public architecture, and little evidence for status differentiation.

instruction: Which of the following are four of the characteristics of civilization?
input:
Options:
A. food surpluses, specialists, urban settlements, and a system of record keeping
B. food surpluses, a standing army, artwork, and a system of plumbing
C. food surpluses, monumental architecture, religious buildings, and museums
D. museums, libraries, monumental architecture, and artwork
output: A. food surpluses, specialists, urban settlements, and a system of record keeping

instruction: Which of the following most strongly indicates advances in the human intellect during the Upper Paleolithic?
input:
Options:
A. parietal and mobiliary art
B. new stone-tool technologies
C. acquisition of non-local raw materials
D. changes in settlement patterns
output: A. parietal and mobiliary art

instruction: With which of the following techniques were the native navigators of the Pacific NOT familiar?
input:
Options:
A. bird flight paths
B. currents and wind patterns
C. magnetic orientation to the poles
D. cloud patterns
output: C. magnetic orientation to the poles

instruction: Recent research with stone tool replication and brain imaging suggests the following hypothesis:
input:
Options:
A. connections made in tool making prepared the brain for the production and use of language.
B. tool making requires cooperation that can only exist with language.
C. tool making originated millions of years after language evolved.
D. connections made between the brain and bipedal locomotion prepared the hands for tool making.
output: A. connections made in tool making prepared the brain for the production and use of language.

instruction: The earliest-known use of bronze is found in:
input:
Options:
A. South America.
B. Mesopotamia.
C. the Indus Valley.
D. China.
output: D. China.

instruction: The New World, “discovered” by Christopher Columbus, was filled with approximately how many people?
input:
Options:
A. 100,000
B. 500,000
C. 1,000,000
D. tens of millions
output: D. tens of millions

instruction: Which of the following sites has monumental earthworks with concentric ridges in a semicircle that date from around 3,500 years ago?
input:
Options:
A. Caral
B. Stonehenge
C. Poverty Point
D. Gobekli Tepe
output: C. Poverty Point

instruction: The controversial theory that people from present-day Europe colonized North America at the end of Pleistocene is:
input:
Options:
A. supported by genetic evidence that establishes close connections between the oldest skeletons in the Americas and the European genome.
B. refuted by genetic evidence from the oldest skeletons in the Americas that establishes close connections between modern Native Americans and the native people of central Siberia.
C. proven by genetic evidence that establishes close connections between the oldest skeletons in the Americas and Norse explorers who arrived in northeastern Canada around A.D. 1000.
D. refuted by the complete absence of documents that record a migration of Europeans into the Americas.
output: B. refuted by genetic evidence from the oldest skeletons in the Americas that establishes close connections between modern Native Americans and the native people of central Siberia.

instruction: What was the required labor service owed to the king in return for the privilege of using property owned by the Incan empire?
input:
Options:
A. Khipu
B. Mit'a
C. Split inheritance
D. Capacocha
output: B. Mit'a

instruction: Archaeology is a subfield of:
input:
Options:
A. biological anthropology.
B. anthropology.
C. cultural anthropology.
D. paleoanthropology.
output: B. anthropology.

instruction: When did the acquisition of raw materials from greater distances increase, and what does it indicate?
input:
Options:
A. during the Upper Paleolithic; long- distance contacts with greater reliance on trade with distant groups
B. during the Middle Paleolithic; the acquisition of raw materials from greater distances indicates people moved more often
C. during the Middle Paleolithic; broader social networks were based on frequent movement for trade and long-distance contacts
D. during the Upper Paleolithic; the importance of higher-quality, imported materials was more widely appreciated
output: A. during the Upper Paleolithic; long- distance contacts with greater reliance on trade with distant groups

instruction: According to the author, what did the Olmec have in common that bound them together in different territories?
input:
Options:
A. underlying religious beliefs, as seen in Olmec art and iconography
B. agricultural surpluses that led to the creation of economic inequalities
C. they spoke the same language and were related by kinship and marriage
D. a system of trade and exchange, as seen in tokens used as a form of money
output: A. underlying religious beliefs, as seen in Olmec art and iconography

instruction: Unlike Mesopotamian writings, the records left by the Maya are principally concerned with:
input:
Options:
A. political and military history.
B. philosophy and religion.
C. trade and economics.
D. astronomy and mathematics.
output: A. political and military history.

instruction: Based on archaeological evidence, which of the following is accurate regarding civilization in general?
input:
Options:
A. The occurrence of warfare decreases as people increasingly invest time in the production of art.
B. The occurrence of warfare is uncommon and occurs only with the concentration of wealth.
C. The concentration of wealth is a common feature.
D. The concentration of wealth is uncommon and occurs only occasionally.
output: C. The concentration of wealth is a common feature.

instruction: Based on the morphology of fossil hominids dating from about 1.8 million until about 400,000 years ago, researchers argue that:
input:
Options:
A. there were two or more related but geographically separate hominid species during this period that evolved from earlier African hominids
B. hominids dating from this time can be grouped into different species in Africa, Asia, and Europe.
C. all of the hominids that evolved from Homo habilis and predate Homo sapiens belong in a single, geographically widespread but morphologically diverse species known as Homo erectus.
D. all of the above
output: D. all of the above

instruction: The evolutionary histories of different kinds of organisms and their relationships to each other are illustrated in a:
input:
Options:
A. diastema.
B. phylogeny.
C. mosaic.
D. genera,
output: B. phylogeny.

instruction: In comparison to an Oldowan tool, a hand axe ____________.
input:
Options:
A. is made out of stone, wood, or bone.
B. needs constant cleaning and maintenance.
C. requires metal and a source of heat to be forged
D. requires many more flakes to be removed.
output: D. requires many more flakes to be removed.

instruction: Homo erectus is most closely associated with which tool-making tradition?
input:
Options:
A. Occipital
B. Acheulean
C. Oldowan
D. Stadial
output: B. Acheulean

instruction: Opportunistic foraging involves:
input:
Options:
A. careful planning and scheduling.
B. reliance on steady sources of food such as shellfish.
C. increased use of imported or "exotic" materials
D. little planning
output: D. little planning

instruction: In rare cases, the residue of blood on ancient stone tools can:
input:
Options:
A. prevent archaeologists from doing their research, since only forensic anthropologists can study bloody tools.
B. be used to identify the species of animals killed and likely eaten.
C. be used to predict the types of weapons that were not used for hunting.
D. none of the above; blood does not preserve and has never been identified on stone tools.
output: B. be used to identify the species of animals killed and likely eaten.

instruction: How were the royal cemeteries of the Moche discovered?
input:
Options:
A. Thieves raiding the tombs were caught by the police.
B. A forest fire burned away the dense vegetation that concealed the cemetery.
C. Archaeologists discovered an exact replica of the city in the map room.
D. A flock of sheep that had been living there fell into a tomb.
output: A. Thieves raiding the tombs were caught by the police.

instruction: The ancient city of Cahokia contained more than _______ and a population of around _______.
input:
Options:
A. 120 earthen mounds; 10,000
B. 60 burial mounds; 2,000
C. 50 religious monuments; 5,000
D. 200 pyramidal mounds; 200,000
output: A. 120 earthen mounds; 10,000

instruction: Based on the analysis of oxygen isotope ratios in the shells of gastropods found in the sediments of an ancient lake, what happened to civilization in the Indus Valley?
input:
Options:
A. It became increasingly complex due to increased rainfall and longer growing seasons.
B. It eventually collapsed due to climate change and drought.
C. It collapsed due to increased monsoons and a series of catastrophic floods.
D. It evolved into a series of city states along rivers and lake shores.
output: B. It eventually collapsed due to climate change and drought.

instruction: Clovis points are NOT found in:
input:
Options:
A. Alaska.
B. Mexico.
C. Canada.
D. the continental United States.
output: A. Alaska.

instruction: Which culture lived a primarily sedentary lifestyle in the Southwest?
input:
Options:
A. Adena
B. Mogollon
C. Kwakiutl
D. Mississippian
output: B. Mogollon

instruction: Lewis Henry Morgan conceived of progress in human culture according to the stages of:
input:
Options:
A. Savagery, Barbarism, and Civilization.
B. Savagery, Civilization, and Collapse.
C. Barbarism, Primitivism, and Civilization.
D. Stone Age, Bronze Age, and Iron Age.
output: A. Savagery, Barbarism, and Civilization.

instruction: By 1900 B.P., the central elements of Mayan culture were in place. These did NOT include:
input:
Options:
A. stratified societies ruled by kings.
B. ritual ball games and a reverence for precious jade.
C. a sophisticated bronze producing industry.
D. a hieroglyphic written language and calendar.
output: C. a sophisticated bronze producing industry.

instruction: Machu Picchu was built in the mountains as a:
input:
Options:
A. defensive stronghold.
B. shrine to the Inca rain god.
C. relaxing getaway for elites.
D. astronomical observatory.
output: C. relaxing getaway for elites.

instruction: What evidence is there that Neandertals were hunters?
input:
Options:
A. Neandertal canine teeth showed that they relied only on meat for their subsistence.
B. Animal bones were found showing stone tool cut marks and no animal teeth marks.
C. Bones of large animals, such as elephant and horse, were found in caves.
D. Both A and C.
output: B. Animal bones were found showing stone tool cut marks and no animal teeth marks.

instruction: Why do we know more about Neandertals than other extinct species of premodern humans?
input:
Options:
A. Neandertals spread throughout the world and their remains are found on every continent.
B. Neandertals used caves in Europe where their remains were preserved.
C. Neandertal populations were larger and more violent than any other premodern humans, whom they drove to extinction.
D. Neandertals left crude but intelligible written records.
output: B. Neandertals used caves in Europe where their remains were preserved.

instruction: The attitude of many ancient elites toward the consumption of resources seems to have been:
input:
Options:
A. “a penny saved is a penny earned."
B. "if you've got it, flaunt it."
C. "look before you leap."
D. "the last shall be first and the first shall be last."
output: B. "if you've got it, flaunt it."

instruction: In 1797, John Frere made a discovery that he described as:
input:
Options:
A. animal remains scattered on the surface of the ground.
B. the earliest written documents.
C. primitive stone tools excavated at great depth.
D. human skulls with ape-like features.
output: C. primitive stone tools excavated at great depth.

instruction: Which of the following first described human culture according to a predictable chronology of a Stone Age, Bronze Age, and Iron Age?
input:
Options:
A. uniformitarianism
B. multilinear evolution
C. three-age system
D. . triple-age catastrophism
output: C. three-age system

instruction: Tiwanaku, with its capital at Titicaca, was one of the ___________ kingdoms of the ancient world.
input:
Options:
A. richest
B. strongest
C. largest
D. highest
output: D. highest

instruction: Monte Alban is located in the ________ and was built by the _________.
input:
Options:
A. Valley of Mexico; Aztec.
B. Valley of Oaxaca; Zapotec.
C. Amazon floodplain; Olmec.
D. Yucatán Peninsula; Maya.
output: B. Valley of Oaxaca; Zapotec.

instruction: In Holocene Africa, the __________ was replaced by the ____________.
input:
Options:
A. microlith blade; backed blade
B. Iberomaurusian culture; Capsian culture
C. Capsian culture; Iberomaurusian culture
D. Maglemosian; Natufian
output: B. Iberomaurusian culture; Capsian culture

instruction: What was NOT a deciding factor in the development of Mesopotamian civilization?
input:
Options:
A. the need to concentrate population away from arable lands near rivers
B. the need to construct monumental works, such as step-pyramids and temples
C. the need to develop a complex social system that would allow the construction of canals
D. the use of irrigation to produce enough food
output: A. the need to concentrate population away from arable lands near rivers

instruction: Which of the following crops was NOT an important component of Hopewell subsistence?
input:
Options:
A. sunflower
B. squash
C. maize
D. knotweed
output: C. maize

instruction: Unequivocal evidence for art as symbolic expression dates from as early as:
input:
Options:
A. 95,000 BP, at Dolni Vestonice.
B. 77,000 BP, at Blombos Cave.
C. 50,000 BP, at Des Moines, IA.
D. 36,000 BP, at Wharton Hill.
output: B. 77,000 BP, at Blombos Cave.

instruction: What was the Chinese technique of stamped or pounded earth that was used in construction of house walls and defensive structures?
input:
Options:
A. Hang-t'u
B. Scapulimancy
C. Lung-shan
D. Qin manufacture
output: A. Hang-t'u

instruction: The Lake Forest Archaic tradition relied on ____________ resources; the Maritime Archaic hunted ___________ creatures.
input:
Options:
A. pelagic; midden
B. lacustrine; pelagic
C. midden; littoral
D. littoral; lacustrine
output: B. lacustrine; pelagic

instruction: Genetic evidence indicates that the modern Inuit are the descendants of which people?
input:
Options:
A. Paleo-Eskimos
B. Dorset
C. Thule
D. Clovis
output: C. Thule

instruction: Which tool technology is associated with anatomically modern Homo sapiens?
input:
Options:
A. Aurignacian
B. Acheulean
C. Mousterian
D. both b and c
output: A. Aurignacian

instruction: What is the difference between an absolute date and a relative date?
input:
Options:
A. An absolute date is known by everyone, while a relative date ranges from 30 to 50 years.
B. A relative date is derived from radiometric dating techniques, while an absolute date is only associated with written documents.
C. A relative date refers to a year or a range of years, while an absolute date indicates a chronological order.
D. An absolute date refers to a year or a range of years, while a relative date indicates a chronological order.
output: D. An absolute date refers to a year or a range of years, while a relative date indicates a chronological order.

instruction: Upon exploring Rhode Island, the Italian navigator Giovanni de Verrazzano noted that the native people resembled:
input:
Options:
A. Italians.
B. Asians.
C. Australians.
D. Melanesians.
output: B. Asians.

instruction: Like the urban centers of the Indus Valley, Teotihuacán appears to have been:
input:
Options:
A. equipped with sophisticated plumbing and cooling systems.
B. subject to constant outbreaks of plague and disease.
C. surrounded by an enormous agricultural hinterland.
D. planned and built on a grid pattern.
output: D. planned and built on a grid pattern.

instruction: The population of the Valley of Mexico was supported by means of:
input:
Options:
A. long-distance trade, salt mining, and stone masonry.
B. hunting and gathering, fishing, and cultivation of root crops.
C. advanced medical, artisanal, and metallurgical technologies.
D. agricultural irrigation, terraces, and artificially raised fields called chinampas.
output: D. agricultural irrigation, terraces, and artificially raised fields called chinampas.

instruction: Which subfield of anthropology has been described as studying "other people's garbage"?
input:
Options:
A. primatology
B. archaeology
C. paleoanthropology
D. linguistics
output: B. archaeology

instruction: What did the Moche build at the heart of their urban center?
input:
Options:
A. a vast complex of temples and artisan workshops
B. an enormous walled-in precinct of elite residences
C. the Pyramid of the Sun
D. the Temple of the Feathered Serpent
output: C. the Pyramid of the Sun

instruction: Mayan city-states were NOT:
input:
Options:
A. ruled by autonomous dynasties.
B. similar in their political organization to Egyptian communities.
C. supported by large agricultural hinterlands.
D. much smaller in population than Mohanjo-daro.
output: B. similar in their political organization to Egyptian communities.

instruction: The argument in favor of hominids making and using stone tools by at least 3.3 million years ago is supported by:
input:
Options:
A. cut marks on animal bones that were made by butchering with pieces of stone.
B. the anatomy of Australopithecus africanus hands and analogies with studies of living non-human primates that demonstrate tool use.
C. simple stone cores, anvil stones, and flakes found at the Lomekwi 3 site in West Turkana, Kenya.
D. all of the above.
output: D. all of the above.

instruction: What do the amounts of rainfall in the Maya homeland, as reflected in variations in oxygen isotopes in a stalagmite in Yok Balum Cave in Belize, correspond to?
input:
Options:
A. increased rainfall and severe flooding that led to the collapse of Maya ceremonial centers
B. severe drought and a decline in construction at Maya ceremonial centers
C. increased rainfall and increased storage of surplus food from agriculture
D. increased warfare and the abandonment of the entire region
output: B. severe drought and a decline in construction at Maya ceremonial centers

instruction: In the author's two-hour movie representing the history of the universe, when do the earliest members of the human family appear?
input:
Options:
A. at the beginning of the film
B. about half way through the film
C. 90 minutes into the film
D. during the final 3 seconds of the film
output: D. during the final 3 seconds of the film

instruction: Which best describes Stonehenge?
input:
Options:
A. Megalithic monument
B. Halafian monumental center
C. Chavin ritual monument
D. Mesopotamian monument
output: A. Megalithic monument

instruction: Which commonly used name for a culture was borrowed from another Native American language and literally means “ancient enemies”?
input:
Options:
A. Kwakiutl
B. Hohokam
C. Anasazi
D. Mogollon
output: C. Anasazi

instruction: Paleogenetic and paleoecological evidence points to dates of occupation for Australia as far back as:
The Egyptian system of hieroglyphics:
input:
Options:
A. did not use pictographs
B. appears to have developed suddenly
C. was the earliest form of writing in the world
D. all of the above
output: B. appears to have developed suddenly

instruction: What do we know about the people who built Stonehenge based on the analysis of animal teeth from a nearby village?
input:
Options:
A. They raised livestock at the site, including cattle, sheep, and goats.
B. They brought animals to the site from outside of the region.
C. They had no domesticated animals but hunted wild animals for meat.
D. They hunted antelope, gazelle, and bear.
output: B. They brought animals to the site from outside of the region.

instruction: Evidence from the modern human genome suggests that genes inherited from Neandertals:
input:
Options:
A. are universally beneficial to modern humans.
B. control the metabolism of fat in modern Europeans.
C. are associated with human diseases such as Lupus.
D. both b and c.
output: D. both b and c.

instruction: The Nazca geoglyphs extend over miles and represent:
input:
Options:
A. entrances to subterranean tombs of the elite.
B. vast architectural designs for cities and towns.
C. ceremonial pathways and effigies of spirits and gods.
D. landing strips for spaceships.
output: C. ceremonial pathways and effigies of spirits and gods.

instruction: The fact that early excavators of Teotihuacán mistook ordinary housing compounds for palaces suggests:
input:
Options:
A. the general standard of living was high.
B. commoners took over the residences of the elite.
C. the city was a democracy, ruled by common farmers and artisans.
D. the society was mostly egalitarian, with almost no social stratification.
output: A. the general standard of living was high.

instruction: Why is the timing of monumental construction at Ceibal significant?
input:
Options:
A. It contradicts the hypothesis that the monumental construction of the Maya was largely inspired by the Olmec.
B. It confirms that the residents of Ceibal were inspired by the Olmec to build large platforms.
C. It contradicts the hypothesis that the development of monumental construction among the Maya was an internal process.
D. It confirms that the Olmec, who built most of the Maya monuments, were inspired by the Egyptians.
output: A. It contradicts the hypothesis that the monumental construction of the Maya was largely inspired by the Olmec.

instruction: The origins of Chinese civilization can be traced to:
input:
Options:
A. the site of An-yang near the Huang ho River.
B. chiefdoms and states in numerous regions throughout China.
C. the beginning of the Qin Dynasty.
D. external influences originating from the Indus Valley.
output: B. chiefdoms and states in numerous regions throughout China.

instruction: How long ago did human groups begin actively controlling their food sources by artificially producing conditions under which these sources would grow?
input:
Options:
A. within the past 6,000 years
B. within the past 12,000 years
C. within the past 18,000 years
D. within the past 28,000 years
output: B. within the past 12,000 years

instruction: For which of the following is there evidence for Neandertals?
input:
Options:
A. Neandertals adorned themselves with pendants and necklaces.
B. Neandertals buried their dead.
C. Neandertals produced and used complex stone tools.
D. All of the above.
output: D. All of the above.

instruction: What occupation date do most archaeologists agree on for Australia?
input:
Options:
A. no earlier than 80,000 years ago
B. soon after 60,000 years ago
C. soon after 40,000 years ago
D. no earlier than 20,000 years ago
output: C. soon after 40,000 years ago

instruction: Which of the following dating techniques are based on the measurement of the amount of energy trapped in materials that have been heated at archaeological sites?
input:
Options:
A. argon/argon and potassium argon dating
B. archaeomagnetic and radiocarbon dating
C. luminescence dating and optically stimulated luminescence
D. X-ray fluorescence and paleomagnetic dating
output: C. luminescence dating and optically stimulated luminescence

instruction: Which tool technology is associated with Neandertals?
input:
Options:
A. Aurignacian
B. Acheulean
C. Mousterian
D. both b and c
output: C. Mousterian

instruction: Conflict models emphasize the importance of __________ tensions in the development of state societies, while integration models emphasize ____________ tensions.
input:
Options:
A. external; internal
B. military; religious
C. internal; external
D. extrafamilial; interfamilial
output: C. internal; external

instruction: Homo erectus differed from Homo habilis in which way?
input:
Options:
A. Erectus fossils are found only in Africa.
B. Erectus possessed a smaller brain.
C. Erectus possessed a larger brain.
D. Erectus was a relatively short-lived species.
output: C. Erectus possessed a larger brain.

instruction: There is general consensus among paleoanthropologists that anatomically modern humans:
input:
Options:
A. migrated out of Africa into western Europe between 150,000 and 200,000 years ago and then spread into Asia, Australia, and the Americas.
B. evolved in Asia between 100,000 and 50,000 years ago, and then migrated into Africa, Europe, Australia, and the Americas.
C. evolved independently and simultaneously in Africa, Europe, and Asia and then migrated into Australia and the Americas.
D. migrated out of Africa into Southwest Asia between 150,000 and 100,000 years ago and then spread into Europe, Asia, Australia, and the Americas.
output: D. migrated out of Africa into Southwest Asia between 150,000 and 100,000 years ago and then spread into Europe, Asia, Australia, and the Americas.

instruction: Homo erectus was:
input:
Options:
A. a stable, long-lived species.
B. an unsuccessful, short-lived species.
C. the first hominid to make and use stone tools.
D. the first hominid to stand “erect” and walk upright.
output: A. a stable, long-lived species.

instruction: About 2.6 to 1.9 million years ago the planet became much _____ and entered the ______:
input:
Options:
A. colder; Pleistocene epoch.
B. hotter; Miocene epoch.
C. colder; Pliocene epoch.
D. hotter; Pleistocene epoch.
output: A. colder; Pleistocene epoch.

instruction: Mayan art and iconography prominently feature depictions of:
input:
Options:
A. infants and children.
B. stars and comets.
C. love and sex.
D. mutilation and violence.
output: D. mutilation and violence.

instruction: Taphonomy is:
input:
Options:
A. a systematic classification based on similarities and differences.
B. a dating technique based on the decay of a radioactive isotope of bone.
C. a study of the spatial relationships among artifacts, ecofacts, and features.
D. the study of how materials ended up in a particular place.
output: D. the study of how materials ended up in a particular place.

instruction: The large, extinct herbivores of the Pleistocene era are referred to as:
input:
Options:
A. megaliths.
B. megafauna.
C. megaflora.
D. megatrons.
output: B. megafauna.

instruction: Recovery of more than 6,500 bones and bone fragments from 28 individuals of a single hominid species at the Cave of the Bones in Spain provides:
input:
Options:
A. little evidence of diversity, since each individual represents a different species.
B. unusually good evidence to examine diversity within a hominid species.
C. evidence of interbreeding between Homo neanderthalensis and Homo erectus.
D. relatively little evidence to examine diversity within the species.
output: B. unusually good evidence to examine diversity within a hominid species.

instruction: Charles Darwin discovered that plants and animals had evolved through a process known as ____________. Early archaeologists discovered that ______________________.
input:
Options:
A. scientific creationism; human culture evolved differently than plants and animals
B. unilineal evolution; civilizations evolved more quickly than plants
C. natural selection; human culture did not evolve or change much over time
D. natural selection; human culture had evolved over an enormous period of time
output: D. natural selection; human culture had evolved over an enormous period of time

instruction: The construction of large-scale features, such as mounds and shell middens, is often taken by archaeologists as evidence of:
input:
Options:
A. the practice of slavery.
B. social and political complexity.
C. a Mesolithic tradition.
D. the shift from Paleolithic to Neolithic.
output: B. social and political complexity.

instruction: The Shang Dynasty laid the foundation for a coherent development of Chinese civilization that lasted well into the:
input:
Options:
A. 10th century.
B. 13th century.
C. 17th century.
D. 20th century.
output: D. 20th century.

instruction: What do Homo sapiens and Australopithecus afarensis have in common?
input:
Options:
A. a mode of locomotion
B. a reliance on brachiation
C. a lack of sexual dimorphism
D. all the above
output: A. a mode of locomotion

instruction: What effect did the late Pleistocene to early Holocene climate change have on human populations?
input:
Options:
A. It forced populations to move toward the equator.
B. It tested the ability of human beings to adapt.
C. It forced humans to wear clothing.
D. It had no effect at all.
output: B. It tested the ability of human beings to adapt.

instruction: Recent discoveries of Homo naledi fossils in the Dinaledi Chamber of the Rising Star cave system in South Africa suggest a mixture of post-cranial morphologies or mosaic of hominid traits. One of the reasons this new species is controversial is that:
input:
Options:
A. there are already two well-known species of Homo and it is unlikely there were more than two species at one time.
B. paleoanthropologists did not make the discovery and it was found in an inaccessible cave in South Africa.
C. there is, as yet, no firm date that can be applied to the specimens.
D. the Homo naledi fossils have been shown to pre-date the earliest known hominid fossils by millions of years.
output: C. there is, as yet, no firm date that can be applied to the specimens.

instruction: A genetic study comparing the bones of a 7,000-year-old skeleton found in Germany, eight human skeletons dating to 8,000 years ago in Luxembourg, and more than 2,300 living Europeans found that the modern European genome included contributions from:
input:
Options:
A. the earliest anatomically modern Homo sapiens who lived in Europe 45,000 years ago.
B. people genetically traceable to the Middle East who moved into Europe about 9,000 years ago.
C. people who moved there from west Asia less than 5,000 years ago.
D. all of the above.
output: D. all of the above.

instruction: Which of the following is archaeological evidence of social stratification and inequality?
input:
Options:
A. Burials without exotic grave goods also contain bones indicating that they engaged in less strenuous labor.
B. Burials with exotic grave goods also contain bones indicating that they engaged in less strenuous labor.
C. Burials all contain equal amounts of exotic grave goods, but some are more impressive than others.
D. Burials contain bones indicating that people were segregated based on gender, stature, and personal capabilities, including artistic abilities.
